questions.stem: A 46-year-old man has 8 months of weakness. It began with trouble turning keys with his right hand and now affects both legs. Exam shows wasting of the small hand muscles, twitching under the skin of the arms and thighs, brisk knee reflexes and extensor plantar responses on both sides. Pin, vibration and position sense are normal in all limbs. Eye movements and bladder function are normal. His mother and her brother died of a similar illness in their 50s. Genetic testing finds a disease-causing mutation. The normal protein made by this gene has which function?
choices: Conversion of superoxide radicals to hydrogen peroxide
Iron handling inside mitochondria
Assembly of RNA-splicing complexes in lower motor neurons
Cleavage of amyloid precursor protein inside membranes
Repair of DNA double-strand breaks
questions.explanation: Mixed **upper motor neuron** signs (hyperreflexia, Babinski) and **lower motor neuron** signs (atrophy, fasciculations) with **normal sensation** indicate **amyotrophic lateral sclerosis**. Among the familial forms (the most common is a C9orf72 repeat, not offered here), some come from mutations in **SOD1**, the copper-zinc **superoxide dismutase** that turns superoxide into hydrogen peroxide; the mutant protein misfolds and damages motor neurons. The SMN protein (RNA-splicing complexes) is tempting, but its loss causes **spinal muscular atrophy**: lower motor neuron signs only, usually starting in infancy, with autosomal recessive inheritance.
questions.explanation_pt: Sinais de **neurônio motor superior** (hiper-reflexia, Babinski) e de **neurônio motor inferior** (atrofia, fasciculações) com **sensibilidade normal** indicam **esclerose lateral amiotrófica**. Entre as formas familiares (a mais comum é uma expansão no C9orf72, que não está entre as alternativas), algumas decorrem de mutações no **SOD1**, a **superóxido dismutase** de cobre e zinco que converte superóxido em peróxido de hidrogênio; a proteína mutante se dobra de forma errada e lesa os neurônios motores. A proteína SMN (complexos de *splicing* do RNA) é tentadora, mas sua perda causa **atrofia muscular espinhal**: só sinais de neurônio motor inferior, em geral com início na lactância, com herança autossômica recessiva.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman has 2 months of drooping eyelids and double vision that appear late in the day. By the end of a meal she also has trouble chewing. Ptosis gets worse after she looks upward for 60 seconds. Pupils react normally. Reflexes and sensation are normal. Test results are: serum acetylcholine receptor antibodies, high; repetitive nerve stimulation at 3 Hz, a progressive fall in the muscle response; thyroid-stimulating hormone, normal. A chest CT is ordered. Which finding is most closely associated with her disease?
choices: Central mass near the hilum of one lung
Enlarged lymph nodes in both hila
Mass at the apex of one lung
Mass in the anterior mediastinum
Mass in the posterior mediastinum
questions.explanation: **Fatigable** ptosis, diplopia and chewing weakness, **acetylcholine receptor antibodies** and a **decremental response** on slow repetitive stimulation indicate **myasthenia gravis**. The **thymus**, which sits in the **anterior mediastinum**, is often abnormal: **thymic hyperplasia** or **thymoma**. A central hilar mass is tempting, but it suggests **small cell lung cancer**, which goes with **Lambert-Eaton syndrome**: proximal leg weakness that improves with effort, low reflexes and dry mouth. An apical (Pancoast) tumor can cause ptosis through **Horner syndrome**, but with a small pupil and no fatigable diplopia.
questions.explanation_pt: Ptose, diplopia e fraqueza da mastigação com **fatigabilidade**, **anticorpos contra o receptor de acetilcolina** e **resposta decremental** na estimulação repetitiva lenta indicam **miastenia gravis**. O **timo**, que fica no **mediastino anterior**, costuma estar alterado: **hiperplasia tímica** ou **timoma**. Uma massa hilar central é tentadora, mas sugere **câncer de pulmão de pequenas células**, associado à **síndrome de Lambert-Eaton**: fraqueza proximal das pernas que melhora com o esforço, reflexos reduzidos e boca seca. Um tumor apical (Pancoast) pode causar ptose pela **síndrome de Horner**, mas com pupila pequena e sem diplopia com fatigabilidade.

questions.stem: A 57-year-old man is brought in by his wife because his personality has changed over 2 years. He tells crude jokes to strangers, has spent much of their savings on sudden purchases and eats large amounts of sweets. He no longer seems to care about his grandchildren. He remembers appointments and recent events well and finds his way around town without help. During the visit he repeats the same phrases and keeps touching objects on the desk. There is no tremor, rigidity or abnormal movement. Brain MRI is most likely to show atrophy mainly in which region?
choices: Hippocampus and medial temporal lobes, then parietal cortex
Frontal lobes and anterior temporal lobes
Heads of the caudate nuclei
Occipital and posterior parietal cortex
Midbrain, with relative sparing of the cortex
questions.explanation: Early **disinhibition**, **apathy**, **compulsive** behavior and **hyperorality** with memory and navigation still intact point to the behavioral form of **frontotemporal dementia**. Its atrophy is concentrated in the **frontal and anterior temporal lobes**. The hippocampal and parietal pattern is tempting, but it belongs to **Alzheimer disease**, which starts with memory loss and getting lost, not with personality change. Caudate atrophy fits Huntington disease, which would bring chorea.
questions.explanation_pt: **Desinibição**, **apatia**, comportamento **compulsivo** e **hiperoralidade** precoces, com memória e orientação espacial ainda preservadas, indicam a forma comportamental da **demência frontotemporal**. A atrofia se concentra nos **lobos frontais e temporais anteriores**. O padrão hipocampal e parietal é tentador, mas pertence à **doença de Alzheimer**, que começa com perda de memória e desorientação espacial, e não com mudança de personalidade. A atrofia do caudado corresponde à doença de Huntington, que traria coreia.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old woman is brought in by her daughter because of 3 months of fast-worsening confusion. She can no longer dress herself, her gait has become unsteady, and her body jerks suddenly when a door slams. She has no fever. Cerebrospinal fluid shows: white blood cells 2/μL (normal 0-5); protein 40 mg/dL (normal 15-45); glucose 64 mg/dL, with serum glucose 98 mg/dL; 14-3-3 protein, positive. EEG shows sharp waves that repeat about once per second. Which process is the cause of her disease?
choices: Reactivation of a latent polyomavirus in oligodendrocytes
Accumulation of α-synuclein in cortical neurons
Persistent measles virus infection of neurons
Autoantibodies against neuronal surface receptors
Misfolded protein that makes the normal protein misfold
questions.explanation: **Rapidly progressive dementia** with **startle myoclonus**, ataxia, **periodic sharp waves** on EEG and a bland CSF with **14-3-3 protein** indicate **Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease**. Abnormal **prion protein** in a **β-sheet** form resists proteases and makes normal prion protein refold the same way, causing **spongiform change** without inflammation. Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (persistent measles) is tempting because it also causes myoclonus and periodic EEG complexes, but it affects children and young adults years after measles and shows high anti-measles antibodies in the CSF. Autoimmune encephalitis usually shows CSF inflammation.
questions.explanation_pt: **Demência rapidamente progressiva** com **mioclonias desencadeadas por sobressalto**, ataxia, **ondas agudas periódicas** no EEG e LCR sem inflamação, com **proteína 14-3-3**, indicam **doença de Creutzfeldt-Jakob**. A **proteína priônica** anormal, em forma de **folha β**, resiste às proteases e faz a proteína priônica normal se dobrar da mesma maneira, causando **alteração espongiforme** sem inflamação. A panencefalite esclerosante subaguda (sarampo persistente) é tentadora porque também causa mioclonias e complexos periódicos no EEG, mas acomete crianças e adultos jovens anos após o sarampo e mostra anticorpos antissarampo elevados no LCR. A encefalite autoimune costuma mostrar inflamação no LCR.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old man with Down syndrome lives in a group home. Over 2 years, staff have noticed that he forgets daily routines he once did well, such as making his breakfast. He now gets lost inside the building, and he recently had his first generalized seizure. Thyroid function tests and vitamin B12 level are normal. His hearing and vision have not changed. Which mechanism best explains why this decline began in middle age?
choices: Inheritance of two APOE ε4 alleles
A presenilin-1 mutation that alters γ-secretase cleavage
An extra copy of the amyloid precursor protein gene
Expansion of a CAG repeat in the huntingtin gene
A tau gene mutation that makes tau aggregate
questions.explanation: The gene for **amyloid precursor protein (APP)** is on **chromosome 21**, so trisomy 21 gives a third copy and more **amyloid-β** production. Alzheimer plaques appear early, usually by about age 40, and dementia often follows in the 40s or 50s; new seizures are common at this stage. **APOE ε4** is tempting because it is the main genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer disease, but it is on chromosome 19 and does not explain the early disease that is typical of Down syndrome. Presenilin-1 mutations cause familial early-onset Alzheimer disease, not the Down syndrome form.
questions.explanation_pt: O gene da **proteína precursora do amiloide (APP)** fica no **cromossomo 21**; por isso, a trissomia 21 fornece uma terceira cópia e aumenta a produção de **amiloide-β**. As placas de Alzheimer surgem cedo, em geral por volta dos 40 anos, e a demência costuma vir entre os 40 e os 50 anos; crises epilépticas novas são comuns nessa fase. O **APOE ε4** é tentador porque é o principal fator de risco genético da doença de Alzheimer de início tardio, mas fica no cromossomo 19 e não explica a doença precoce típica da síndrome de Down. Mutações da presenilina-1 causam Alzheimer familiar de início precoce, e não a forma da síndrome de Down.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man is brought to the clinic 1 week after he injected a synthetic opioid made in a home laboratory. Within days he became very slow and stiff. Temperature is 37.0°C, pulse is 82/min and blood pressure is 124/78 mm Hg. He has a masklike face, rigidity in all limbs, a resting tremor of both hands and a shuffling gait. Serum creatine kinase is normal. Analysis of the drug shows a contaminant that was converted in his brain into a toxic product, which destroyed dopamine neurons of the substantia nigra. Which enzyme carried out this conversion?
choices: Catechol-O-methyltransferase
DOPA decarboxylase
Tyrosine hydroxylase
Monoamine oxidase A
Monoamine oxidase B
questions.explanation: The contaminant **MPTP** crosses the blood-brain barrier, and **monoamine oxidase B** in astrocytes converts it to **MPP+**. The dopamine transporter carries MPP+ into nigral neurons, where it blocks **mitochondrial complex I** and kills them, causing permanent **parkinsonism**. Monoamine oxidase A is the most tempting choice, but it mainly breaks down serotonin, norepinephrine and dietary tyramine; MAO-B inhibitors such as selegiline prevent MPTP toxicity in animal studies. Normal temperature and creatine kinase argue against neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
questions.explanation_pt: O contaminante **MPTP** atravessa a barreira hematoencefálica, e a **monoamina oxidase B** dos astrócitos o converte em **MPP+**. O transportador de dopamina leva o MPP+ para dentro dos neurônios da substância negra, onde ele bloqueia o **complexo I mitocondrial** e os destrói, causando **parkinsonismo** permanente. A monoamina oxidase A é a alternativa mais tentadora, mas degrada principalmente serotonina, noradrenalina e tiramina da dieta; inibidores da MAO-B, como a selegilina, impedem a toxicidade do MPTP em estudos com animais. Temperatura e creatinoquinase normais afastam a síndrome neuroléptica maligna.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis has received natalizumab infusions for 3 years. Over 6 weeks she has developed trouble finding words, clumsiness of the right hand and weakness of the right leg. She has had no fever or headache. MRI shows large white matter lesions in the left frontal and parietal lobes; they do not enhance with contrast and cause no mass effect. Cerebrospinal fluid shows: white blood cells 3/μL (normal 0-5); protein 48 mg/dL (normal 15-45); PCR for JC virus DNA, positive. Which action of her drug most directly allowed this infection?
choices: Depletion of B cells through binding to CD20
Blockade of α4 integrin on circulating lymphocytes
Retention of lymphocytes in lymph nodes via S1P receptors
Inhibition of pyrimidine synthesis in dividing lymphocytes
Reduced T-cell activation through interferon-β signaling
questions.explanation: **Natalizumab** is an antibody against **α4 integrin**, so lymphocytes cannot bind the vessel wall and enter the brain; this lowers **immune surveillance** of the CNS. Latent **JC virus** can then reactivate and kill **oligodendrocytes**, causing **progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy** with non-enhancing white matter lesions. Anti-CD20 therapy is tempting because rituximab is also linked to PML, but that is not how natalizumab works.
questions.explanation_pt: O **natalizumabe** é um anticorpo contra a **integrina α4**; assim, os linfócitos não conseguem aderir à parede vascular e entrar no encéfalo, o que reduz a **vigilância imunológica** do SNC. O **vírus JC** latente pode então se reativar e destruir **oligodendrócitos**, causando **leucoencefalopatia multifocal progressiva** (LEMP) com lesões da substância branca sem realce. A terapia anti-CD20 é tentadora porque o rituximabe também se associa à LEMP, mas esse não é o mecanismo do natalizumabe.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy has 3 years of a worsening, wide-based, unsteady gait, and he now falls often. His parents are healthy; his older sister developed the same problem at a similar age. He has had no more infections than other children. Exam shows slurred speech, high-arched feet and mild scoliosis. Ankle and knee reflexes are absent, but both plantar responses are extensor. Vibration and position sense are lost in the feet, and the Romberg test is positive. His eyes and skin look normal. Which additional finding is most likely?
choices: Recurrent sinus and lung infections with low IgA levels
Golden-brown rings at the edge of the cornea
Cataracts with myotonia and frontal balding
Left ventricular hypertrophy on echocardiogram
Wasting and twitching of the tongue muscles
questions.explanation: Teenage-onset gait **ataxia** with **areflexia**, **Babinski signs**, loss of **dorsal column** sensation, **pes cavus**, scoliosis and an affected sibling indicate **Friedreich ataxia**, an autosomal recessive **GAA repeat** in the frataxin gene. Loss of frataxin disturbs mitochondrial iron handling, and **hypertrophic cardiomyopathy** is common and is the usual cause of death. Ataxia-telangiectasia is the most tempting alternative, but it starts in early childhood with ataxia, later adds eye telangiectasias and frequent infections, and it does not cause cardiomyopathy. Kayser-Fleischer rings (Wilson disease) do not come with absent reflexes and dorsal column loss.
questions.explanation_pt: **Ataxia** de marcha iniciada na adolescência, com **arreflexia**, **sinal de Babinski**, perda da sensibilidade das **colunas dorsais**, **pé cavo**, escoliose e um irmão afetado, indica **ataxia de Friedreich**, uma expansão autossômica recessiva de **repetições GAA** no gene da frataxina. A perda da frataxina altera o metabolismo mitocondrial do ferro, e a **cardiomiopatia hipertrófica** é comum e é a causa habitual de morte. A ataxia-telangiectasia é a alternativa mais tentadora, mas começa no início da infância com ataxia, depois surgem telangiectasias oculares e infecções frequentes, e não causa cardiomiopatia. Os anéis de Kayser-Fleischer (doença de Wilson) não vêm com arreflexia e perda das colunas dorsais.
